detail: Use reverse-chronological sections: appointments, education, publications (flag peer-reviewed venues and first/senior authorship), grants with amounts and your role, teaching, supervision, service and invited talks. Keep the master version long, then trim per call.

Use a tabular format with exact dates (MM/YYYY). A professional photo is optional but still common, and personal data such as nationality is usual. Include separate sections for Lehrerfahrung (course title, semester, SWS, role, evaluation scores), Drittmittel and Gremienarbeit (committee work).
Name the post reference, the department's research groups you would connect with, 2–3 courses you can teach and your funding plan. Rewrite the first and last paragraphs for every application.

item: Supporting statement mapped to the person specification
detail: UK/Irish shortlisting scores you against each Essential/Desirable criterion. Use the criteria as headings (e.g., 'E3: Evidence of securing research funding') with 2–4 lines of concrete evidence each, and never skip one.

Mark venue type and rank (e.g., NeurIPS/ICML/FAccT, Phil Sci, Cognitive Science), open-access links and your contribution. Many EU calls (DE, NL, CH) ask for the '5 most important publications' with a 3–4 line justification each.

German, Austrian, Italian, Spanish and Hungarian calls often require copies of PhD and Master's certificates. Keep PDF scans of the Edinburgh PhD certificate ready (and certified translations where needed, e.g., for Spanish/Italian procedures).

Open with a one-paragraph vision (e.g., a science of AI evaluation and explanation, drawing on philosophy of science and cognitive science). Then 2–3 threads, each with past results and future questions, ending with why this department.

Set year-by-year goals: first PhD students in Y1, a first major grant in Y1–2 (ERC StG / NWO Veni/Vidi / UKRI / SNSF), group size targets and flagship outputs. Committees in DE, NL, CH and the Nordics expect a concrete plan, not just themes.

List specific named schemes with eligibility windows: ERC StG (2–7 years post-PhD), MSCA, UKRI FLF, EPSRC New Investigator, Emmy Noether, Veni/Vidi, SNSF Starting Grant, Villum/WASP-HS, Academy of Finland, plus AI safety funders (e.g., Open Philanthropy, UK AISI grants). Show 1–2 already applied for or won.

Pick 3–5 outputs and write a 100-word statement for each on originality, significance and rigour, as UK REF panels do. Note impact potential (policy uptake, e.g., in AI regulation/standards) as a possible impact case study.
Tabulate each grant or fellowship with funder, period, amount, your role (PI/co-I) and success status. German committees weigh this heavily, so include smaller travel and compute grants too.
Many European calls require uploading full texts. Use camera-ready or published versions, with the file name including the year and venue.

Give your philosophy with concrete examples: active learning, assessment design and a module you would build (e.g., 'AI Safety & Interpretability' or 'Philosophy of Science for AI'). Name existing courses in the department's curriculum you can teach immediately.

Include syllabi, student evaluation scores, peer observation reports, supervision list (BSc/MSc/PhD) and a reflective section. Nordic countries treat pedagogical merit as a formal criterion scored by external experts.

UK: an HEA Fellowship / PGCert (often required during probation). NL: the BKO/UTQ (required within 1–2 years, so list prior training that may be recognised). Nordic: university pedagogy courses (10 weeks in SE, 200 hours in NO). Say where you stand for each.

State explicitly that you will obtain the BKO (Basiskwalificatie Onderwijs) within the probation period, and cite any recognised prior training (e.g., CMU Eberly Center teaching programs) to shorten the route.

Prepare a 20–30 min Bachelor-level lecture that can be adapted to a set topic. Include an interactive element and clear learning objectives. It is a separate scored part of the Berufungsverfahren (DE/AT/CH) and of Nordic procedures (provföreläsning).
List co-supervised PhD students, MSc/BSc theses and interns, with names, outcomes and placements. Formal co-supervision matters for later habilitation/Docent titles and Nordic promotion.
Mix a PhD advisor (Edinburgh), a postdoc PI (CMU) and 1–2 external senior people who know your work. UK/Irish calls often contact referees only at shortlist, often within 48 hours, so warn them.

Send each referee your CV, research statement, the job ad and key points to emphasise (e.g., independence, teaching, AI-safety leadership). Highlight UK REF/impact angles for UK letters and grant potential for EU letters.
German/Austrian calls use external Gutachten, and Nordic calls use sakkunniga. Keep a list of conflicts of interest (co-authors, advisors) ready, because you may be asked to declare them.
UK posts often ask how you will advance Equality, Diversity and Inclusion (Athena SWAN context). Give concrete actions (inclusive teaching, outreach, mentoring) rather than values alone.
State your current level (CEFR) and a timeline to teach in the local language (German, Dutch, Danish, Swedish or French), e.g., B2 in 2 years. Committees and contracts often require it.

Register for MCF qualification in the autumn via Odyssée (the deadline is usually in Oct), then submit the dossier in Dec–Jan. Check whether a foreign Assistant Professor-equivalent post exempts you. Missing it costs a year.

Write a 3–5 page combined research and teaching concept tailored to the Denomination (the chair's named field). Explain how you will integrate with the faculty's Profilbereiche (focus areas) and existing Sonderforschungsbereiche (DFG collaborative research centres).
US-style, ambitious 5-year vision: focus on fundamental questions and how you will build a group of 5–8. Mention links to ETH AI Center, the Swiss AI Initiative or EPFL AI Center.
Dutch calls increasingly want a narrative CV (NWO style) covering team science, open science, public engagement and leadership, not just metrics. Prepare a 1-page narrative version.

UK: check whether your EUSS status from the Edinburgh PhD years is still valid, or plan for Global Talent. NL: 30% ruling eligibility. DK: forskerordning (researcher tax scheme). SE: expertskatt. BE: inbound-researcher regime. Ask HR at offer stage.

Lead with impact: key papers with a one-line result each, open-source tools, models evaluated and compute scale. Add a skills section (PyTorch, JAX, evals, interpretability tooling). Drop teaching and service.

Research-scientist loops (Google DeepMind, Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta FAIR, Microsoft Research) include 1–2 Python coding rounds: LeetCode medium-level, data manipulation, or implementing ML components (e.g., attention, a training loop) from scratch. Practise under time pressure.
Tailor the job talk to the lab's agenda (e.g., interpretability, evals, alignment science). Show concrete results, how the method scales, and what you would do in the first 6 months.

item: ML system design / research design rounds
detail: Practise designing an evaluation pipeline, an interpretability study or a red-teaming system end to end: data, metrics, confounds, compute and failure modes. Metascience expertise on eval validity is a differentiator.
Clean GitHub repos with READMEs for key papers, reproducible notebooks and a personal website. Industry reviewers check these.

Know London/Zurich/Paris research-scientist ranges (base, bonus, equity) from levels.fyi. Industry offers can be used to negotiate start-up or salary in academia (especially CH/NL), and academic offers can do the same in industry.
The UK AI Security Institute and EU AI Office (and national AISIs) hire research scientists with policy-relevant evaluation skills. Expect work tests or take-home tasks instead of LeetCode.
Prepare 20 min (UK panel day), 30–45 min (DE Vorsingen, CH/Nordic) and 60 min (ETH/EPFL, industry) versions. Aim the first 5 minutes at non-specialists.

Rehearse: your research vision in 2 minutes, the first grant you will write, how you will attract PhD students, teaching you'd take on, contribution to department citizenship and EDI, and why this place. UK panels ask nearly identical question sets.

Draw up a written list before the Ruf covering Leistungsbezüge, WiMi positions (permanent vs fixed-term), Sekretariat, start-up, lab space, compute, teaching reduction and dual-career support. Once you accept, leverage disappears.

UK: ask for a higher spine point, a first-year teaching reduction, a PhD studentship and relocation. NL: scale step and 30% ruling. CH/ETH: start-up and positions. Everywhere: start date and dual-career support.
Email the head of group or chair of the committee with a short note and CV. It is normal in the UK, NL, Nordics and FR, where local fit and prior contact matter a lot.
First-round interviews in NL, the Nordics and the UK are often online. Test your camera, lighting and a backup connection, and time-zone-check slots from Pittsburgh (often 6–9am EST).
